spec.title: Select verification by the behavior affected

selection.title: 1. Choose proof before paying for a build

p.MINIMUM-SUFFICIENT-PROOF: The ordinary atom default is the smallest set of checks that proves its affected behavior, ordinary negative cases, invariants and named dependent interfaces. Select by the actual change and contract consumers, not by the total size of the project. Two changed classes do not imply rebuilding or running every test in their packages. Preserve applicable schema, code-generation, security and other independent oracles; narrow execution, not the obligations being proved.

p.SELECT-BEFORE-DISPATCH: Before dispatch, identify affected claims, their producing code and contract consumers, then name the build/test target and exact test or small module family that can prove them. Inspect source and existing commands first; a planned test is a recipe to implement, not a command already available. Refresh this selection against the real diff before acceptance, including any newly affected consumer. Do not guess executable commands or test filters from a task id or a proposed test name.

p.SELECTION-NOTE: Retain a short selection note in the existing packet or evidence: claim; changed subject and named consumer; target, filter, flags, fixtures and consequential environment; expected selected cases; rough build/run cost; and the condition that would invalidate the evidence or require wider scope. A few lines are enough; unknown cost is recorded as unknown, not measured by first running the full panel. This adds no required plan field, file, queue or harness scheduler.

p.COMMAND-REFINEMENT: When an existing packet or plan names a broader command than this policy requires, the coordinator may replace it with narrower commands that demonstrably cover the same affected claims. Record the old scope, replacement and claim-to-proof mapping in ordinary evidence; preserve task ids, acceptance obligations and campaign-specific fields. This authorized procedure correction does not require another owner permission. It does not silently cancel an explicit request for a full panel or the designated comprehensive final campaign gate.

targets.title: 2. Narrow the compilation target as well as the test filter

p.TARGET-FIRST: For Cargo, select the package and target before the runtime filter: `--lib` for library unit tests, `--test NAME` for a named integration-test binary, `--bin NAME` for a named binary target, and `--doc` only when affected documentation examples require it. Then select the exact test, with the test harness's `--exact` when appropriate, or a justified small module family. Include every required case in the chosen proof. A filter alone can still compile unrelated targets, so it is not by itself a sufficient scope selection. Apply the equivalent target-first rule to other build systems. A selected monolithic target can still compile many tests; do not claim that a runtime filter avoids that cost. If measured target structure prevents economical verification, record the bounded build/test organization problem for the coordinator instead of silently widening the run or undertaking an unrelated test reorganization.

p.DISCOVERY-COST: Use code search and available build metadata to discover target and test names before executing a test runner. If listing is necessary, list only the selected target; Cargo `--list` still incurs compilation for the targets selected. A global test list, unfiltered `cargo test -p PACKAGE`, workspace tests or `--all-targets` is not an ordinary discovery or fallback command. The same commands are allowed only when their actual breadth has been justified by the scope ladder below.

p.NONVACUOUS-SELECTION: Verify that the expected cases actually ran and asserted the intended behavior. A successful exit with zero selected tests is not a behavioral-test pass; neither are compile-only evidence, setup failure or a wrapper that loses the child exit status. A compile check proves its own compilation claim, not test behavior. If the expected case is missing, correct the target/filter or supply the missing targeted test. Do not respond by running everything merely to obtain a green result.

p.BUILD-ARTIFACT-REUSE: Reuse compatible incremental build and dependency artifacts, including the existing Cargo target directory when toolchain, configuration and concurrent access permit. Do not run `cargo clean`, create a cold target directory or commission duplicate builds by default. Isolation required for correctness has an explicit reason and bounded scope. Include compilation cost in selecting the proof. A reusable build artifact saves compilation; it is not evidence that a test passed.

p.NONPRODUCT-CHANGES: A documentation, comment or planning-only change normally needs its affected format, reference, schema or documentation checks, not product Rust suites. Executable examples, generated inputs or normative contract changes can affect product behavior; identify that concrete effect and select its tests instead of relying solely on the file extension.

scope.title: 3. Widen only to resolve a specific missing proof

facts.SCOPE-CASES: Start with exact affected cases or a small named family, including required negative and invariant cases.
facts.SCOPE-CONSUMERS: Add named integration consumers where an interface, schema or generated artifact changed; identify the contract each consumer test proves.
facts.SCOPE-COMPONENT: Run the affected component suite when its shared behavior or unresolved coverage makes the smaller proof insufficient. Explain what this wider run will establish.
facts.SCOPE-PRODUCT: A whole-product panel is justified by an explicit full-panel request, the designated comprehensive final campaign gate, or demonstrated crosscutting impact for which no adequate narrower proof exists. Name the impacted product and the coverage gap; do not expand a leaf-package check to an unrelated host product.

p.NOT-SCOPE-TRIGGERS: Completing an atom, making a commit, a worker/model/session change, a milestone label, pushing or publishing, touching a public surface, or changing several crates does not by itself trigger a full panel. Review the actual effect and any genuinely owed gate. The final comprehensive campaign gate remains required; local atom checks alone do not satisfy that gate.

p.WORKER-SCOPE-BOUNDARY: A worker stays within its named verification perimeter. Missing context, a failed command or uncertain coverage is reported with the missing claim and smallest proposed next proof; it is not permission to self-escalate to a component or workspace suite. The coordinator may choose the next bounded scope under existing owner authority. Routine selection creates no new owner permission ritual.

evidence.title: 4. Reuse valid steps and resume the unfinished panel

p.STEP-SUBJECT: A reusable verdict names its actual relevant input closure: source and generated inputs, dependencies, fixtures, schemas, configuration, command and flags, toolchain, build target and consequential environment. Reuse only while that subject matches and the same claims and cases were actually covered. A whole-repository HEAD change alone does not invalidate unrelated proof; an unchanged HEAD alone cannot establish validity. If the closure is unknown, rerun that affected step, not automatically every check.

p.PANEL-RESUMPTION: When a declared fail-fast panel stops, preserve its complete required step/case denominator and inspect surviving results before rerunning. On the current acceptance subject, replay failed, interrupted or invalidated steps and the unrun tail; reuse earlier passing steps only when their relevant input closures remain valid. Reuse must preserve every required case within each step, not just a green step label. If validity cannot be established, replay the necessary steps; replay the entire panel only when that entire scope is owed and no prior step remains provably valid.

p.AGGREGATE-CLAIM: Evidence assembled from compatible per-step runs may prove the complete declared gate on the acceptance subject. Report it as an aggregate, with each required step/case mapped to its result, omissions explicitly unresolved, and inherited evidence identified. Do not say the full script passed in one invocation if it did not. If the gate actually depends on one uninterrupted order or shared state, that dependency is part of its subject and must be reproduced; do not splice incompatible runs.

p.NO-PREREQUISITE-DELAY: Shared evidence may serve several atoms when the complete proof applies to each. Do not defer a prerequisite check until after the dependent action it guards, collapse away distinct claims, or use artifact-cache hits as test verdicts. A new failure or changed subject invalidates the affected proof and reopens that work.
